To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the median lethal time of Syrian hamsters exposed to aerosolized plutonium oxide was 4-6 months; that the median lethal dose of 239Pu in the lungs was 4,000 rads, and that the median lethal lung dose of 238Pu was about 1,000 rads.

the incidence of lung tumours in Syrian golden hamsters following inhalational exposure to 239PuO-2 is significantly less than that observed in the same species following inhalation exposure to 238PuO_2-ZrO_2 particles.

the incidence of lung tumours in Syrian golden hamsters exposed to aerosolized 238PuO(2)-ZrO(2) particles was significantly higher than the incidence of lung tumors in Syrian golden hamasters exposed to aerosolised 239PuO(2) particulates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of inhaled plutonium on the lung.
the development of an inhalation model for studying the carcinogenic effects of inhaled particles.
the effects of inhaled plutonium aerosols in Syrian hamsters, with the emphasis on the carcinogenic effects of the plutonium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no significant difference between the tumour incidences produced by 239PuO 2 and 238PuO 2-ZrO 2 particles.
the tumour incidence is not significantly different from the spontaneous incidence in the Syrian hamster.
the incidence of lung tumours in Syrian golden hamsters exposed to 239PuOx aerosols was low, but that it was not zero.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incidence of pulmonary tumours in Syrian golden hamsters is related to the initial lung dose of the 239PuO 2 particles.
the lung tumour incidence is dependent upon the type and size of the particles, the initial lung burden and the time of observation after the exposure.
there is an increased incidence of tumours in the lung and in other organs of Syrian hamsters following exposure to aerosolized 238PuO 2-ZrO 2 or 239PuO 2 particles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lung tumour incidence in hamsters is highly sensitive to the particle size and composition of the plutonium aerosol.
plutonium oxide particles can cause tumours in the lungs of Syrian hamsters but at doses that are much higher than previously thought.
there is a significant difference in the lung tumour incidence between the two aerosols.
